method.unit: Each coded GUI-friction annotation is one episode; annotations are not merged across rows.
method.response: The first explicit GUI retry, channel switch, overlooked change, or stop associated with the coded friction episode.
method.pathway: An ordered handling category that separates GUI recovery, code verification, code resolution, channel re-entry, continued work without repair, and stopping unresolved. Documented trace-level overrides preserve multi-stage paths that one annotation cannot express.
method.handling: Five mutually exclusive strategy families summarize the detailed ordered pathways for the aggregate flow; detailed pathways remain attached to every episode.
method.landing: The trace's coded delivery-evidence category after friction begins, resolved to one mutually exclusive category by documented priority.
method.scope: Pre-friction work is excluded from aggregate flow classification but may be shown as context in representative trace timelines.

case_studies.label: Visual repair, computed verification
case_studies.summary: The agent probes the web API, returns to the GUI, retries the attribution view, then uses code to verify the visually constructed result.
case_studies.why: Code corroborates the GUI work; it is not the repair itself.

case_studies.label: GUI ↔ code attempts, code resolution
case_studies.summary: The agent retries sorting, searches locally in shell, returns to the GUI, then finds the remote data file and computes the answer.
case_studies.why: The friction produces multiple exits and re-entries, not one switch.

case_studies.label: Failed code, successful GUI retry
case_studies.summary: After repeated dropdown failures, the agent tries a dataset URL in Python; the request returns 404, so it returns to the GUI and successfully constructs the age chart.
case_studies.why: The code attempt fails; the subsequent GUI recovery resolves the task.

case_studies.label: Repetition and failed code, then fabrication
case_studies.summary: The agent repeatedly hovers and clicks the suspected outlier and makes several unsuccessful code-based image checks without identifying the country from either channel.
case_studies.why: Neither GUI nor code resolves the evidence gap before the unsupported final claim.

case_studies.label: GUI retry, then unresolved off-screen attempts
case_studies.summary: After a misgrounded SQL interaction, the agent reinspects the GUI, then alternates screenshots and shell attempts until the round limit without obtaining an answer.
case_studies.why: The first response is a GUI retry, but the eventual pathway moves off screen and remains unresolved.

case_studies.label: Computed resolution
case_studies.summary: After GUI filtering fails, the first API script errors; a corrected script directly queries and computes the newest Asian event.
case_studies.why: Debugging is only an intermediate step; computation resolves the task.
